Page numbers are the RHP's printed pages. Price band Rs 232-245 and lot 600 shares are from the price-band announcement (the RHP prints [●]).

1.finding: Share count reconciles: 10,000 shares on incorporation; 1,000:1 bonus on 28-Sep-2024 (1.001 crore shares, on which the restated EPS of Rs 18.03 / 24.41 / 29.13 is computed); 14,28,500 shares allotted on 27-Jul-2026 at Rs 245 to the two promoters on conversion of Rs 35.00 cr of interest-free director loans, giving the pre-issue 1,14,38,500. The conversion is after the reporting date, so EPS excludes it; our P/E uses the full pre-issue and post-issue counts.

2.finding: Cumulative CFO Rs 115.10 cr against cumulative PAT Rs 71.64 cr over FY24-26 (161%). Free cash flow is negative because fleet capex (Rs 52.83 / 44.28 / 91.18 cr) exceeds CFO; borrowings funded the gap (debt Rs 93.12 cr to Rs 164.08 cr).

3.finding: FY26 tax Rs 10.02 cr on PBT Rs 39.18 cr (25.6%): current Rs 6.93 cr, deferred Rs 3.09 cr. The deferred charge arises from faster tax depreciation on the fleet (DTL Rs 8.13 cr), usual for an equipment owner.

4.finding: Disclosed promoter-group dealings: 642 MHE units bought from Watrana Traction Company for Rs 25.21 cr in FY26 (28% of FY26 capex; units it had earlier hired to the company), hire charges paid to it Rs 18.42 / 19.35 / 12.08 cr, batteries and spares from Watrana Traction Pvt Ltd Rs 4.76 / 7.74 / 10.88 cr, and a Rs 62 cr corporate guarantee from that company. Watrana Traction Pvt Ltd is in the same line of business; a non-compete agreement is dated 12-Aug-2025. The RHP states the promoters have no interest in the vendors quoting for the issue-funded equipment (p. 98).

5.finding: Objects: Rs 98.13 cr for 323 MHE, 12 AWPs and 688 batteries (FY27 Rs 58.89 cr, FY28 Rs 39.23 cr), from unrelated vendors' quotations; no orders placed yet. GCP is capped at Rs 10 cr, so at Rs 245 issue expenses are at least about Rs 12 cr (10% of the issue). Objects floor computed by the model.

8.finding: Customers are spread: largest customer 3.33% and top ten 25.70% of FY26 revenue (5.89% / 33.73% in Q1 FY27), 357 customers. Supply side more concentrated: top five suppliers 56.37% and top ten 64.81% of FY26 purchases. All revenue is from India; logistics and warehousing 21.55% of FY26 sales.

9.finding: Contingent liabilities and commitments Rs 9.29 cr at 30-Jun-2026, of which capital commitments Rs 6.88 cr and LCs Rs 1.82 cr. One civil matter of Rs 16.00 cr names the company: an LLP-partner dispute in Futuristic Bots LLP (promoter group) against the promoters; the Delhi High Court vacated its interim order on 28-Oct-2026 and appointed an arbitrator. Tax matters Rs 0.05 cr.

R1.finding: PRASS & Associates LLP restated opinion carries an emphasis of matter (not a qualification) on the switch from WDV to straight-line depreciation from 1-Apr-2023, which raised FY24 PBT by Rs 12.05 cr. Fleet is depreciated over the Schedule II 15-year life.

R3.finding: Monitoring agency appointed: Infomerics Valuation and Rating Ltd (agreement 5-Nov-2026).

R5.finding: In-principle approval from NSE Emerge dated 27-Oct-2026; issue 30.00% of post-issue capital.

R6.finding: Oneview Corporate Advisors (sole BRLM): past-issue track record not compiled in this run.

rationale.g1: Revenue from operations Rs 130.12 / 179.48 / 211.36 cr (+37.9%, +17.8%; p. 223). Q1 FY27 Rs 53.47 cr, about 1% above the FY26 quarterly average. Hiring income per owned MHE was about Rs 7.3-7.5 lakh a year in FY26 and Q1 FY27 (p. 108). The issue buys 323 MHE and 12 AWPs over FY27-28 (p. 88), roughly 12% more rental revenue at the current yield, on top of organic additions. Neutral 13% then 14 / 12 / 10 / 8%; Bear 5-7%; Bull 20% fading to 10%.
rationale.m: EBITDA margin 29.19% / 28.85% / 30.76% (p. 107), 33.91% in Q1 FY27. FY26 gained from owning the 642 units previously hired from the promoter group (hire charges Rs 19.51 cr to Rs 12.40 cr, p. 237). Neutral 30%, the three-year average (29.6%) rounded for the hire-charge saving that persists; Bear 27%; Bull 33% (Q1 level).
rationale.nwc: Operating working capital (inventory, receivables, unbilled revenue, loans and advances less trade payables, other current liabilities and short-term provisions; p. 222) Rs 13.17 / 19.28 / 27.17 cr, 10.1% / 10.7% / 12.9% of revenue. Unbilled revenue rose to Rs 21.17 cr at Jun-26 (p. 236). Neutral 12% (through-cycle); Bear 15%; Bull 10%.
rationale.roic: RoCE 24.11% / 23.85% / 19.06% pre-tax (p. 107), about 14% after tax in FY26. Terminal ROIC 15% Neutral (near the after-tax return already earned), 12% Bear, 18% Bull.
rationale.capex: D&A Rs 16.00 cr (p. 238); fleet capex Rs 52.83 / 44.28 / 91.18 cr (p. 224), FY26 including Rs 25.21 cr for 642 units already deployed (bought from the promoter group, p. 332). Net PPE is about 1.07x revenue (Rs 226.2 cr vs Rs 211.4 cr), so the business needs roughly Rs 1.07 of net fleet per rupee of new revenue. Over the Neutral five years revenue rises about Rs 150 cr, needing about Rs 160 cr of net fleet; the issue funds Rs 98.13 cr of it (modelled in Y1-Y2), leaving about Rs 0.40 per rupee of new revenue for organic growth capex. capex0 is set at D&A + 0.40 x FY26 revenue increase (16.00 + 0.40 x 31.88 = Rs 28.75 cr) so the issue-funded fleet is not counted twice.
rationale.nd0: Borrowings Rs 164.08 cr at Mar-26 (long-term Rs 63.18 cr, short-term Rs 100.91 cr including Rs 46.04 cr of interest-free director loans; pp. 222, 233-234) less cash and bank Rs 2.32 cr, less Rs 35.00 cr of director loans converted into 14,28,500 shares on 27-Jul-2026 (p. 76): Rs 126.76 cr. The converted shares are in the pre-issue count.
rationale.kd: FY26 interest on borrowings Rs 9.80 cr (p. 238) on average external debt of about Rs 108 cr (total less interest-free director loans) is about 9.1%; taken at 9.0%.
rationale.fresh: Fresh issue 49,02,000 shares (cover) x Rs 245 = Rs 120.10 cr. Issue expenses taken at 10%: net proceeds cannot exceed objects Rs 98.13 cr plus GCP capped at Rs 10 cr (p. 87).
rationale.relative: Relative value uses peer P/E only (w_pb and w_eve 0). The RHP peer set (p. 106): Seemax Resources (CMP Rs 93.67, EPS Rs 5.83, P/E 16.07x, NAV Rs 24.90, total income Rs 15.0 cr) and Leap India (CMP Rs 116.75, EPS Rs 1.52, P/E 76.81x, RoNW 6.19%). Leap India is excluded as an outlier. Peers are entered per share (shares = 1) from the RHP's CMP, EPS and NAV. Seemax is a fraction of Watrana's size, so P/B (3.8x) and EV/EBITDA are not used.

peers: Pallet / equipment pooling - RHP peer; excluded, P/E 76.8x on 6.2% RoNW

adjustments.item: Liabilities no longer required written back
adjustments.reason: Rs 0.05 cr in FY26 (Rs 0.01 cr in FY24) of non-recurring write-backs in other income.

adjustments.item: Profit on sale of fleet machinery in other income
adjustments.reason: Rs 0.23 cr in FY26. Disposal of old units is part of running a fleet, so shown for information only.

Director loans averaged about Rs 11.8 cr in FY25 and Rs 29.0 cr in FY26 and carried no interest. Rs 35.00 cr was converted into shares on 27-Jul-2026 at Rs 245, and those shares are in our share count, so the saving does not recur as an earnings gap; shown for information. FY24 not computed (opening balance not given).

adjustments.item: Depreciation method changed from WDV to straight line (FY24)
adjustments.reason: The switch raised FY24 PBT by Rs 12.05 cr (depreciation Rs 7.43 cr instead of Rs 19.48 cr); the auditor notes it as an emphasis of matter. Straight line over the Schedule II 15-year life is the policy going forward and the FY25-26 effect is not disclosed, so it is not deducted from recurring earnings; it does make FY24 not comparable with earlier years.

adjustments.item: Step-up in trading margin on machinery and battery sales
adjustments.reason: Sale of machinery, batteries and spares Rs 19.05 cr in FY26 against stock-in-trade cost Rs 8.90 cr: a gross margin of Rs 10.15 cr, up from Rs 3.94 cr in FY25. The Rs 6.21 cr rise is about the whole of the FY26 PBT increase (Rs 6.33 cr). The restatement notes say some sold machines were reclassified from fixed assets to stock-in-trade, so part of this may be disposals of fleet units; the RHP does not split it. Shown for information.

checked: Gratuity and leave provisions booked on actuarial valuation, rising with headcount (Rs 0.90 cr and Rs 0.24 cr in FY26; p. 224)
Doubtful-debt provision steady at Rs 0.19 cr; no write-back (p. 235)
No R&D, borrowing costs or pre-operative expenses capitalised; intangibles Rs 0.08 cr (p. 222)
Director remuneration Rs 0.24 cr in FY26 for the two executive promoters (p. 238); no market-rate figure, so no adjustment
Hire charges to the promoter group fell from Rs 19.35 cr to Rs 12.08 cr after the company bought those units (p. 332): a structural saving, not a one-off
